reading.body:
QTS Hillsboro 1 publishes 20 MW of IT capacity at 22271 Broderick Drive. At 40 kW per rack, a common assumption for AI training density, 20 MW of IT load is roughly 500 racks. At 10 kW per rack, a common assumption for general enterprise colocation, the same 20 MW supports roughly 2,000 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so the actual rack count depends on the workload mix, which is not disclosed.

No certifications are listed in the published specifications, so no certification-based conclusions about qualified workloads can be drawn.

Oregon has 133 facilities mapped in this site's data, of which only 6 publish a megawatt figure, together totaling 182 MW. Hillsboro 1's 20 MW represents roughly 11 percent of that published total, placing it fifth among the six facilities with a published figure. The remaining 127 mapped facilities publish no capacity number, so the true scale of Oregon's data center footprint is larger than the 182 MW figure reflects, by an unknown amount. Hillsboro sits in Washington County, which hosts a significant concentration of Oregon data center activity, though the extent of that concentration relative to other counties is not calculable from the facts available here.
